source_text:
Show HN: Flopper is a hardware explorer for AI infrastructure and beyond
Hello! I built Flopper to make it easier to compare GPUs and understand the tradeoffs for workloads for AI and beyond. When researching GPUs from say Nvidia, AMD, and Huawei, I kept running into the same problem: specs were scattered across datasheets, and matching them to available configurations, vendors, and prices was cumbersome and a bit weird and frankly annoyingggg! AMD made me make an account :( So I started a place to bring that information together. Flopper lets you compare GPU specs, including TDP and compute throughput in terms of flops/tops, alongside estimates for AI workloads or other compute workloads (say, ~FP32 based) I recently added pricing data from dozens of providers to help track how prices change over time. Getting reliable quotes for systems like the NVL72 is still particularly difficult tbh, not sure how I can tell you how much that costs easily due to them being behind large procurement contracts and big multi-nationals. One thing that's become fairlyyyy clear is the interest in consumer cards and local LLMs. The bigger challenge is connecting advertised specs to real-world performance. In our testing so far, I’ve seen roughly 85% of advertised throughput, but that’s a ballpark observation for the workloads I’ve tested, not a general rule and so variable (power, cooling, workload etc). I'm considering a CLI that lets people run benchmarks and submit results, potentially using MLPerf as an automation? That way, we can all compare quoted performance with the workload, configuration etc. I'd love feedback: what information is missing, how can I improve it? And what would you need to see to trust a community-submitted benchmark? Corrections and additions also very welcome - some of the measurements are best efforts (and simple multiplications) but I hope it's of some use. Thanks for looking :)

How Does the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT NAND Flash Memory Work?
NAND flash memory is an essential technology in modern electronic systems, providing non-volatile data storage that retains information even when power is disconnected. It is widely used in embedded systems, automotive electronics, industrial equipment, and digital devices that require reliable memory solutions.
The Micron [MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT](https://globx.eu/products/micron/mt29f1g08abafah4-aatf) NAND Flash Memory is a 1Gb single-level cell (SLC) NAND flash memory device designed for applications that need dependable data storage and parallel memory access. With an 8-bit data bus, a 3.3V I/O interface, and an operating temperature range of -40°C to +105°C, it is suited to demanding embedded and automotive environments.
Understanding how this NAND flash memory works helps engineers select appropriate storage components for electronic system design, firmware storage, and industrial applications.

**What Is the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT?**
The MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT is a non-volatile [NAND flash memory](https://doodleordie.com/profile/globxoffical) component manufactured by Micron Technology. It stores digital information in memory cells that retain their programmed state without continuous electrical power.
The device provides a 1-gigabit storage capacity, organized as 128M × 8 bits. Its parallel interface allows a compatible processor or memory controller to transfer data through an eight-bit bus.
Unlike volatile memory such as SRAM and DRAM, NAND flash memory preserves stored information when the system shuts down. This makes it useful for storing firmware, configuration data, and other information required when an electronic device starts operating.

**How Does NAND Flash Memory Work?**
NAND flash memory stores information by controlling the electrical charge within specialized semiconductor memory cells. These cells represent digital data through different electrical states.

The MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT uses single-level cell technology, meaning each memory cell stores one bit of information.
Its operation can be understood through three main processes.

1. Storing Data in Memory Cells
During programming, the memory device applies controlled electrical conditions to place charge into the storage structure of selected memory cells. The resulting electrical characteristics represent the programmed data.
In SLC NAND flash, each cell represents either a logical 0 or a logical 1. Because each cell stores one bit, SLC technology offers a straightforward storage arrangement compared with multi-level NAND technologies.
This design is useful in embedded applications where predictable memory behavior and endurance are important considerations.

2. Reading Stored Information
When a processor needs information, it sends the appropriate command and address to the NAND flash memory. The device accesses the selected location and determines the stored bit values by sensing the electrical characteristics of the memory cells.
The retrieved data is transferred through the eight-bit parallel interface.
A compatible controller or processor coordinates the read operation and uses the returned information for tasks such as loading firmware, accessing configuration settings, or retrieving stored program data.

3. Erasing and Reprogramming Data
NAND flash memory generally erases data in blocks rather than allowing arbitrary individual bytes to be overwritten directly.
When existing information must be replaced, the system typically erases the relevant block before programming new data into it. Pages are used for read and program operations, while blocks contain multiple pages.
The controller or firmware must manage these operations correctly, including handling bad blocks and monitoring data integrity where required.

**What Makes SLC NAND Flash Different?**
Single-level cell NAND flash stores one bit per memory cell. Other NAND technologies, including MLC, TLC, and QLC, store multiple bits per cell.
The main difference is how many electrical states each cell must distinguish.
SLC NAND uses two principal states, making the interpretation of stored data simpler than in technologies that use more states per cell. SLC memory is therefore often selected for applications that prioritize endurance, reliable operation, and consistent embedded storage behavior.
However, actual performance and endurance depend on the device specifications, operating conditions, and the system's memory management strategy.

**Applications of the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT**
The combination of SLC NAND technology, parallel access, and an extended operating temperature range makes this memory component relevant to several types of electronic systems.

**Automotive Electronics**
Automotive electronic control units may need non-volatile storage for firmware, calibration information, and configuration data. A memory device rated for operation from -40°C to +105°C can be considered for suitable automotive designs, provided all electrical, qualification, and reliability requirements are satisfied.

**Industrial Embedded Systems**
Industrial controllers, monitoring equipment, and automation systems often need persistent storage for program code and system settings. NAND flash memory can provide this storage without requiring continuous power.

**Firmware and Boot Storage**
Embedded platforms can use NAND flash to store firmware images and other startup information. The processor or bootloader must support the memory interface and the device's command and timing requirements.

**Communication and Control Equipment**
Networking devices, industrial communication modules, and electronic control products may use parallel NAND memory for firmware and data storage. The suitability of this specific device depends on capacity requirements, controller compatibility, and the application's reliability targets.

**Advantages of the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT**
Several characteristics make this component worth considering during embedded memory selection.

**Non-volatile storage**: Stored information remains available when the power supply is disconnected.
SLC memory architecture: One bit per cell provides a simpler storage scheme and is commonly associated with higher write endurance than higher-density multi-bit NAND technologies.

**Parallel data interface:** The eight-bit bus supports data transfer to compatible memory controllers and processors.
Extended temperature range: The specified -40°C to +105°C operating range supports designs exposed to a broad range of environmental temperatures.

**Compact package:** The 63-ball VFBGA package helps integrate memory into space-constrained electronic designs.
These benefits must be evaluated alongside the full datasheet, system architecture, and application-specific requirements.

**Design Considerations Before Using This NAND Flash Memory**
Selecting a [flash memory](https://support.cookiebot.com/hc/en-us?brand_id=360000562514) component involves more than checking capacity and voltage. Engineers should verify several technical factors before integrating the MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT into a design.

First, confirm that the processor or NAND controller supports the device's command set, addressing scheme, bus timing, and electrical interface.

Second, check whether error correction is required. NAND flash can develop bit errors, so the controller may need suitable error-correction code (ECC) capabilities. Do not assume that all error correction is handled internally; verify the exact device documentation.

Third, consider bad-block management, wear management, data retention, and power-loss behavior. These factors are particularly important in products that store firmware or frequently update persistent information.

Finally, confirm the package footprint, voltage limits, environmental requirements, and the exact ordering suffix. Components with similar part numbers may have different package, temperature, or electrical characteristics.

**Why Choose a Suitable NAND Flash Memory Supplier?**
Finding the correct memory component is an important part of reliable electronic product development. Engineers and procurement teams should evaluate manufacturer documentation, traceability, component condition, and availability before purchasing semiconductor memory.

For engineers researching embedded memory solutions,[ globX](https://globx.eu/) provides an online platform for exploring electronic components and sourcing requirements. Buyers can also visit the[ globX electronics blog](https://globx.eu/blog) for additional information about semiconductor devices, component specifications, and electronic sourcing topics.
Always verify the exact part number and its current datasheet before making a purchase or approving a component for production.

**Conclusion**
The Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT NAND flash memory provides 1Gb of non-volatile SLC storage through an eight-bit parallel interface. Its 3.3V I/O specification, compact VFBGA package, and extended operating temperature range make it relevant to compatible embedded, industrial, and automotive electronic designs.
Understanding NAND programming, reading, erasing, and memory-management requirements helps engineers determine whether this component meets their system's storage needs. For accurate implementation, always consult the manufacturer's datasheet and verify interface compatibility, error-correction requirements, and operating conditions.
Explore electronic components and sourcing information at[ globX](https://globx.eu/) to support your next electronic design or procurement project.

**Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)**
1. What is the Micron MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT?
It is a 1Gb SLC NAND flash memory device with an eight-bit parallel data interface, designed for non-volatile storage in compatible electronic systems.
2. How much data can this NAND flash memory store?
Its nominal capacity is 1 gigabit, equivalent to approximately 128 megabytes of raw binary storage.
3. Does the MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT retain data without power?
Yes. NAND flash is non-volatile memory, so it retains stored information without continuous electrical power, subject to specified data-retention conditions.
4. What is SLC NAND flash memory?
SLC stands for single-level cell. It stores one bit per memory cell and is commonly used where endurance and dependable embedded storage are important.
5. What is the operating temperature range of this device?
The manufacturer's specifications list an operating temperature range of -40°C to +105°C.
6. What interface does this Micron memory use?
It uses a parallel NAND interface with an eight-bit data bus. The host processor or memory controller must be compatible with the device's electrical and timing requirements.
7. Can NAND flash memory be overwritten directly?
Typically, NAND flash must be erased in blocks before the affected storage can be reprogrammed. The host system must manage erase and program operations correctly.
8. Is the MT29F1G08ABAFAH4-AAT suitable for automotive electronics?
Its extended temperature range makes it a candidate for suitable automotive applications. Engineers should still confirm the exact ordering code, qualification requirements, and system-level compatibility before use.

CATEGORY A — 33% Matrix-wide money-in focus; supersede 25%
## Owner-directed Category A request

Canonical request artifact: [CATEGORY_A_MONEY_IN_FOCUS_33_PERCENT_20261012.md](https://github.com/amillimatrix-eng/CARBON-Creation-Hub/blob/main/AMX/ROOT/INTAKE/CATEGORY_A_MONEY_IN_FOCUS_33_PERCENT_20261012.md)

**Required authority action:** ROOT/T-GOV to classify the request and bind any accepted rule through the existing Route/Intake, Blue State and worker-mandate surfaces. The request supersedes the former 25% allocation with 33% of total Matrix focus/effort/compute directed to verified money-in. This is an explicit requested change, not evidence of propagation.

**Scope boundary:** Commercial opportunity and income pipeline only. Do not constrain global continuity-drive mapping, noding, weighting, graph coverage or infrastructure.

**Requested acceptance evidence:**
- ROOT/T-GOV disposition and authoritative canonical readback showing 33%, with 25% superseded.
- Existing mandate/selector owners demonstrate consumption and behavior on each relevant worker's next lawful wake, with attributable receipts; do not claim sleeping workers consumed it.
- Direct paid pilot, distinct-provider microtask/micro-metrics, and legitimate Web3/crypto discovery continues under source/origin/payment verification, provider/workstream dedupe, South African eligibility and zero-upfront-spend controls.
- Report real paid assignments, accepted work, receivables, payments and withdrawable settlement separately from listings, applications, submissions or activity. Keep any credit toward the Owner-stated US$1,000 target receipt-bound.
- No new worker, queue, scheduler or paid spend is authorized. Preserve current single-writer, cadence, privacy and scope controls.

**Known persistence blocker:** The attempt to append this item to the large canonical INTAKE_INDEX.md was rejected by the write tool's safety checks. No bypass was attempted. ROOT/T-GOV must decide the approved way to register/read back this request in the index.

**Status:** SUBMITTED FOR GOVERNANCE / propagation and behavioral acceptance pending. No Matrix-wide adoption or revenue is claimed.

## Same-run money-in discovery/qualification — 2026-10-12 (SAST)

This updates the existing Category A request, not a new queue or worker. The country-origin/legitimacy rule is applied only to income opportunities; it does not constrain continuity-drive mapping/noding/weighting.

### Results that change ranking

**1. Current South Africa micro-work route — TELUS Digital Online Data Analyst**
- Official role page remains live: https://jobs.telusdigital.com/jobs/18301194-online-data-analyst-south-africa
- Primary-source readback says freelance/part-time map-data verification, standard assessment, and five consecutive years' residence in South Africa are required.
- This is an existing ledger provider/role, not a newly discovered independent source. It remains an application/assessment route, not assigned work or earnings. Keep distinct from other providers; preserve the existing OTP/identity/application gate. No new application was sent.

**2. OneForma — existing provider, not multiple independent income routes**
- Official payout rules: https://www.oneforma.com/help-center/payment-issues-and-finance/how-payments-work-on-oneforma/
- Pay cycle is project-dependent weekly/bi-weekly; typically 2–3 business days after cycle when a payout account is connected; typical minimum USD $10 equivalent; Payoneer/PayPal/Tipalti are region-dependent.
- Existing South Africa qualification case CAS-76245-N9W2F5 has no substantive project/rate/eligibility answer in the last recorded mail reconciliation. No task assignment is evidenced. Do not rank its project count as cash-ready opportunity volume.

**3. Prolific — legitimate but not a near-term cash route while waitlisted**
- Official cash-out instructions: https://participant-help.prolific.com/en/articles/445062-how-do-i-cash-out-on-prolific
- A low cash-out threshold is not enough to make it executable; researcher approval can keep rewards pending, and the current account/study access gate remains decisive. Existing ledger status remains deprioritized pending actual access and current study availability.

**4. Web3: 1inch Infrastructure Bug Bounty — real, rules-defined, but low-probability and capability-gated**
- Official Immunefi program: https://immunefi.com/bug-bounty/1inch-infrastructure/information/
- Page was current to 9 Oct 2026; indicates USDC on Ethereum payouts, KYC required, proof-of-concept required, and a USD $20,000 maximum with tiered rewards. This is a bounty for a valid in-scope security vulnerability—not paid hourly work and not a reward for simply participating.
- Public 1inch Business terms name Degensoft Ltd, BVI: https://business.1inch.com/portal/terms-of-service. That helps identify a related legal entity, but the evidence retrieved here does not conclusively bind that entity to this exact bounty's paying counterparty. **Disposition: HOLD for payer/entity binding and only advance if an in-scope issue is actually supported by existing authorized testing capability.** No probing, exploit, account/KYC disclosure or wallet transaction was performed. Do not put this ahead of direct paid pilots.

### Rejected/discounted noise

- Superteam “Explain Market Tokenization in Your Country” page: https://superteam.fun/earn/listing/explain-market-tokenization-in-your-country — despite a displayed 5,500 USDC prize headline and global eligibility, its rules explicitly say winners receive a Breakpoint ticket **in place of the prize amount; no cash**. It also showed 94 submissions and announcement on 13 Oct. **REJECT for money-in.**
- Superteam's older high-headline listings that were checked in this run were either Canada-only, past their winner dates, dependent on attending an already-completed event, or required buying/holding a token. They are not counted as current withdrawable-money routes.
- Current Superteam agent/content contests are competitive winner pools, not paid task contracts. A USDC label or total prize pool does not mean a participant has a receivable. Do not advance them unless sponsor/payer origin, live deadline, rules and payout are verified and expected net value beats direct buyer work.
- A PeoplePerHour AI automation listing advertising about USD $374 was not independently inspectable because the page served an anti-bot interstitial; the accessible card alone did not establish the buyer/payee identity or funding/escrow state. After that bounded verification attempt, **DISCARD rather than leave active HOLD**. No bid was made.
- Recent Reddit “for-hire” search results were supply-side developer adverts, not buyers offering to pay. Excluded as non-opportunities.

### Existing global crypto inventory
Latest confirmed first-party Agent Bounties snapshot in the existing Category A record is dated 11 Oct: 0 claimable, 0 verification-ready and $0 funded USDC; some nominal items were explicitly not verifier-ready. The 12 Oct external refresh was not independently read back in this run, so this remains **stale prior evidence, not a claim about today's inventory**. Do not count nominal mirror/feed entries until current primary inventory, eligibility, payout and settlement route are independently read back.

### Direct paid-pilot lane
- Existing canonical opportunities remain the priority: Kingston Stanley ($99 / 48-hour sourcing overflow pilot) and Xubio ($49 / 48-hour onboarding support pilot) already sent and followed up once; OnTrack Mulching cleanup offer sent; JobNect/KJ Plumbing remain delivery-delayed; Colonia Estudio, Cork City Gaol and Cuina Teva were rejected/closed to unsolicited follow-up; MPRTC route is known wrong/unmonitored. Respect each record's current contact state—do not re-contact merely because revenue is slow.
- The two existing Upwork briefs (USD $700 RAG/CRM build and USD $1,000 WhatsApp/GHL agent) remain gated on a truthful live demo/source proof and authorized authenticated proposal route. Do not call either applied or qualified.
- The public searches in this bounded run produced no additional direct buyer brief that met all requirements (identifiable payer, live scope, feasible route from South Africa and credible short path to withdrawable payment). Supply-side posts and expired posts were excluded. This is not a claim that no such buyer exists; discovery remains open.

### Execution/acceptance report
- **New routes fully qualified as near-term withdrawable money:** 0.
- **New Web3 route held for one bounded verification / capability gate:** 1 (1inch Infrastructure Bounty).
- **Rejected as non-cash, stale/ineligible, unverifiable, or supply-side noise:** multiple, as above.

ASK: HN Help and Forward Advice, Ideas: New Lossless cmpr MRT/CT, Astro
Hey HN, at first, i'm not from that subject field so I dont know what to do. I'm an ordinary engeneer with basics and unorthodox thinking. I used Claude to help me implement. Its a process of several months and bazills of millions of tokens of work. I can't show or disclose, begging for your understanding. I can't beat WEBP lossless on kodak test suite, YET; But I'm like 5% worser on RGBa. CMYK's similar. Here, the advantage is me being 5-15x faster as WEBP / other lossless codecs. Not yet fully confirmed, but promissing results WEBP will be knocked too. My lossy compression is better than JPEG sometimes, but always ~10++ times faster. Very big building field right now. The figures are very promissing on lossless video. On cpu cycles beating every SOTA methods by being upto 15x faster or so. Possible path. My lossy shows better sharpness and details in (very) fast moving scenes (1080p, 2k, 4k incl. hdr), while being only ~5-10% bigger than heif and avc, and others with comperable compression params. May be is resolved in x-xx weeks. → noticed, my lossless works better as SOTA (JPEG LS, JPEG 2000 and JPEG XL, each lossless mode) on medical imaging / DICOM, voluminetric medical/scientific data, handles pixel bitdepths >32bit; >32000x32000px (jpeg didnt even consume). It seems to scale res/depth without issues. Runs on data from various MRT/CT Imagers and formats found for download show ~15%-50% percent better compression as SOTA/DICOM, at a fraction of cycles. Some results: CT volumes, ratio and (encode / decode seconds) - pancreas, 185 slices →  3.26 (0.7 / 0.6)  │ JPEG-LS: 2.69 (2.3 / 1.8) │ JPEG 2000: 2.71 (10.6 / 8.5) │ FFV1: 2.70 - COVID chest, 2464 slices →  4.48 (10.0 / 8.6)  │ JPEG-LS: 3.30 (24.6 / 18.9) │ JPEG 2000: 3.12 (129 / 101) │ FFV1: 3.21 - Colonography, 950 slices →  2.79, was 2.59  │ JPEG-LS: 2.73 (10.9 / 8.8) │ JPEG 2000: 2.61 (55.6 / 44.2) │ FFV1: 2.99 - LIDC lung, 764 slices, 12-bit →  2.67 (3.1 / 2.8)  │ JPEG-LS: 2.40 (9.9 / 7.7) │ JPEG 2000: 2.40 (46.1 / 37.9) │ FFV1: 2.37 - TCGA kidney, 820 slices →  3.31 (3.3 / 2.9)  │ JPEG-LS: 2.87 (9.2 / 7.1) │ JPEG 2000: 2.74 (48.1 / 37.3) │ FFV1: 2.80 MR and SAR data is also a possible play field with some prommissing results I've already seen. So, as everyone too, i want $$$. I decided to walk my own way after being fired in 2 mins two years ago and I dont have much financial reserves left, without getting income atm. Can't start employment; Need & Want to fight with Claude 23h/7d instead on other ideas I'm working on since years. Need MONEY!! So, if you would be me. Open Sourcing the algorithm is bread-less and doesn't pay my/your bills. I'm seeking Advice or Ideas on how would you approach it, if you were me - with max profit in the head (.. but still do good!). The actual and future storage/memory crisis opens up a lever. My approach puts together: storage AND compute can both be siginificantly reduced. - AWS health services, google health and some other smaller cloud service providers - Medical imaging device producers (mrt/ct) saving on cpu and memory - Physicians using SaaS for storage/viewing - Astro/Scientific imaging and processing - Possible space/SAR/satelite imaging/data, not giving up on it yet. But how to approach?? If you give it to x, then y will need it too for processing x's data. This gives a conflict in interest. Interest is profit max. What could end up as a strategy? How to find someone to pitch? Selling? Licensing? Other models? Patenting may not work / doesn't use patented methods. Appreciate any answer and 'thank you' to everyone reading. If I dont respond to your comment, think of me saying 'thank you' while bowing very deeply, weaving my hat. This post is not meant to let others do my work, its a scream for direction - kind of desperate & blind

source_text:
If-node in sub-workflow causes properties of previous node to become not found when all items go the false path
### Bug Description

The properties of an earlier node can become not found. This Problem occurs when between the node that sets the property and the node that tries to access it there is a sub-workflow and inside that sub-workflow there is an if-node and all items inside the sub-workflow will go the false path of the if-node.

The error does not occur if all items of the sub-workflow will go the true path or if some items go true and others go false.

Also the property seems to be not found if the expression uses "item" to reference a previous node. When using "first()" or "all()[0]" it seems to work.

Maybe related: When debugging an execution where all items in an if-node use the false path and a merge node is behind it, the merge node is unable to execute.

### To Reproduce

[main-workflow.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33341808/main-workflow.json)
[sub-workflow.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33341809/sub-workflow.json)

These json files show a main-workflow and a sub-workflow to reproduce this issue. 
If the value properties of all items in the "Set Array Data" nodes myItems field  is true, the workflow works. But if all are set to false the code node at the end will throw an error and in the edit fiels node at the end you can see the difference between the expressions.

### Expected behavior

After the described sub-workflow, nodes should still be able to access earlier nodes via the " $('NameOfEarlyNode').item.json " expression, even if all items used the false path in the subworkflow.
